question: Can hipOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor serve as an oracle for the counter-derived RDNA LDS model, then distinguish the model's scope on CDNA?
answer: No. After correcting a blocks-versus-waves unit error in the registered gate, the runtime API reproduces five of seven counter points and misses exactly the two odd-WGP cases. The gfx942 result is retained but cannot be interpreted as a hardware allocation-granule measurement.

pre_registration_correction.original_wording: blocks_per_multiprocessor reproduces the committed waves_per_cu; each row equals workgroups_per_wgp
pre_registration_correction.problem: Those quantities have different units. A 64-thread RDNA block contains two wave32 waves, and the probe already emitted both blocks_per_multiprocessor and waves_per_multiprocessor.
pre_registration_correction.corrected_gate: waves_per_multiprocessor reproduces the gfx1151 counter-derived waves per CU within 0.1
pre_registration_correction.why_this_is_not_selected_after_seeing_th: The conversion is fixed by block_threads=64 and the independently reported warp_size=32. No footprint, threshold, prediction or observed value chooses the factor of two; it is dimensional bookkeeping.

stage_one.required: all seven dimensionally matched API waves_per_multiprocessor values reproduce the gfx1151 counter-derived waves per CU within 0.1

failure_pattern.10752_bytes: counter 10.97 (~11) versus API 12: fail; this is the preregistered falsification footprint

stage_one.interpretation: The API exposes blocks per compute-unit multiprocessor from a 65536-byte dynamic-LDS budget. The counters exposed a 131072-byte pool shared by a two-CU workgroup processor; converting that WGP count to waves per CU preserves odd workgroup counts. The API cannot represent those odd shared-pool cases: it overpredicts the 11-wave footprint as 12 and underpredicts the 9-wave footprint as 8.

cross_architecture_observation.gfx1151_and_gfx1201: All twelve blocks_per_multiprocessor rows are identical despite multiProcessorCount being 20 and 32 WGP respectively.
cross_architecture_observation.gfx942: All twelve blocks_per_multiprocessor rows are also identical to RDNA; only waves_per_block changes from 2 on wave32 to 1 on wave64.
cross_architecture_observation.what_six_means: It is floor(65536 / 10752) for the requested dynamic allocation. Because stage one rejected the API as an oracle for the counter model, six does not establish a 128-byte CDNA hardware allocation granule.
cross_architecture_observation.stronger_pattern: For every architecture and every row, blocks_per_multiprocessor equals floor(65536 / requested_footprint). The API does not expose the counter-derived 1024-byte static-allocation rounding used by the PEPS kernel model.

model_scope_after_this_test.still_supported: For the static PEPS kernel on measured RDNA parts: effective = ceil(footprint/1024)*1024; workgroups per WGP = floor(131072/effective); waves per CU = workgroups per WGP.
model_scope_after_this_test.not_supported: Using hipOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor as a counter substitute, or extending the 1024-byte granule to CDNA from this probe.
model_scope_after_this_test.next_falsification: A CDNA hardware counter for waves/occupancy on a static-LDS kernel, or a documented compiler/code-object LDS allocation field for gfx942. Without one, stop here.

limitations: The probe uses dynamic shared memory while the committed PEPS counter measurements use static __shared__; their disagreement is the result, not something to average away.
No profiler is installed on the gfx942 container, so no CDNA counter cross-check exists.
This result does not change any PEPS latency, checksum, or the RDNA occupancy ceiling.
